functional_compartments.name: Superior (oblique) compartment
functional_compartments.function_note: More horizontally-oriented fibers; documented separate neuromuscular compartment with a distinct moment-arm contribution to external rotation vs. the inferior compartment.
functional_compartments.source: Fabrizio PA, Clemente FR (2011) J Anat 219(3):303-310 (infraspinatus regional compartmentalization)

motor_endplate_zones.reference_line_from: the medial border of the scapula
motor_endplate_zones.reference_line_to: the greater tubercle of the humerus
motor_endplate_zones.method: modified Sihler's staining, with injection evaluation in fresh-frozen cadavers
motor_endplate_zones.notes: The source divides the muscle mediolaterally into five sections and finds the endplate zone mainly in section B, the medial two-fifths, with the centre of the muscle the second most common site. Recorded here as 20-40% of a medial-to-lateral line; the source states the section as 'approximately 20-40% proximal to the muscle' while also calling section B the medial 2/5, so the band's medial edge could be read as 0% rather than 20%. Confirm against the paper's figure before planning a needle from the medial end. This zone runs across the muscle's width, so it applies to both the superior and the inferior compartment.
motor_endplate_zones.source: Lee HJ, Lee JH, Yi KH, Kim HJ, 'Anatomical analysis of the motor endplate zones of the suprascapular nerve to the infraspinatus muscle and its clinical significance in managing pain disorder', J Anat 243(3):467-474 (2023), doi:10.1111/joa.13868 -- 20 specimens, modified Sihler's staining. Retrieved via PubMed.

trigger_points.location_description: Point in the medial belly, just caudal to the scapular spine
trigger_points.referred_pain_pattern: Refers anteriorly: deep pain “inside” the front of the shoulder/anterior deltoid, radiating down the antero-lateral arm and radial forearm, sometimes to the radial hand; less often to the supero-medial scapular border and suboccipital area. Classic mimic of C5-C6 radiculopathy and of biceps/anterior-cuff pathology.
trigger_points.activation_perpetuating_factors: Cannot reach behind the back (bra/back pocket -- combined extension-internal rotation), painful sleep on either side, fatigue/ache with overhead work; loss of external-rotation strength endurance.
trigger_points.notes: The most frequent shoulder trigger-point muscle: active trigger points reported in 77% of chronic shoulder-pain patients in a blinded series.
trigger_points.source: Simons, Travell & Simons Trigger Point Manual -- as cited in this atlas's uploaded shoulder muscle reference document (Donnelly JM, Fernandez-de-las-Penas C, Finnegan M, Freeman JL (eds), Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction: The Trigger Point Manual, 3rd ed., Wolters Kluwer, 2019)
